label: Hodge Structures
notes: Open by announcing the appendix's job: turn the topological data of a Kahler manifold into the linear-algebraic object that complex geometry actually computes against. The deck follows printed pages 155 through 159. A Hodge structure of weight n is the canonical decomposition of complex cohomology by holomorphic type.

label: Defining Decomposition
notes: Restate the definition cleanly. A pure Hodge structure of weight n on a finite-dimensional rational vector space V is a direct-sum decomposition of its complexification into bigraded pieces indexed by (p,q) with p+q=n, satisfying the conjugation symmetry exchanging (p,q) with (q,p). The integer h to the (p,q) is the Hodge number.

label: Hodge Diamond
notes: Draw the Hodge diamond for a compact Kahler surface. The vertical axis indexes total weight; the rows index p plus q. Symmetries h to the (p,q) equals h to the (q,p) reflect across the vertical; Serre duality reflects across the horizontal. Each lattice point is a Hodge number, and the diamond is the bookkeeping tool for cohomology dimensions.

label: Hodge Filtration
notes: Introduce the equivalent filtration data. Define F to the p as the direct sum over r at least p of H to the (r,n-r). The filtration is decreasing, and the original decomposition is recovered by intersecting F to the p with the conjugate F to the (n-p). For variations of Hodge structure the filtration is the holomorphic invariant; the decomposition is not.

label: Polarization
notes: Recall the polarization. A polarized Hodge structure of weight n carries a bilinear form Q satisfying the two Hodge-Riemann relations: orthogonality of distinct (p,q) pieces and positivity of the i-power factor on the primitive part. Polarization is what makes Hodge theory rigid; it produces positive-definite quadratic data.

label: Examples
notes: Walk through small examples. Weight one: an elliptic curve has H to the (1,0) of dimension one over H to the (0,1) of dimension one. Weight two: a K3 surface has Hodge numbers 1, 20, 1. Weight n general: a Calabi-Yau n-fold has h to the (n,0) equal to one. The examples should make the bookkeeping feel concrete.

label: Applied Lab
notes: Run the lab. Pick a small Hodge diamond, perturb h to the (p,q) by one, and ask which Hodge symmetries break: conjugation, Serre duality, or both? Use this as the appendix's invariant-protection drill. The lab keeps the linear-algebraic data inspectable before the more serious variation-of-Hodge-structure machinery enters.

label: Recap
notes: Close by tying the pieces together. A Hodge structure is decomposition data on cohomology; the diamond is its picture; the filtration is the holomorphic shadow; polarization is the rigid extra; examples show how dimensions encode geometry. The next appendix sharpens these notions for Hodge theory in full.
